turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because I just can’t seem to get things in order anymore. My kitchen table is covered with my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center, and all these half-finished lists I make. I sit down to sort it out, and I don’t know what to do first… and before I know it, the whole day is gone.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient describes being unable to organize papers and lists, not knowing what task to prioritize, and losing the day while attempting to sort them.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been having trouble remembering recent things?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I have. I miss returning calls, or I’ll find a bill still sitting under a stack of mail when I thought I had handled it. I’ve forgotten errands I told my daughter I would do. And with my husband’s appointments, more than once I realized too late that I never called to confirm one. It’s been happening a lot.

symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient reports repeatedly forgetting to return calls, handle bills, complete promised errands, and confirm appointments.

turns.doctor_question: When you were a child, did you also have a lot of trouble staying organized?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I did. I remember even in grade school my teachers would say I was bright, but careless. I’d forget books or homework, and they’d have to remind me to finish my seatwork before I could go outside. It was something that came up more than once.

symptom_reasoning.S001: She reports that teachers described her as bright but careless repeatedly in grade school.
symptom_reasoning.S004: She recalls needing reminders to finish seatwork before being allowed to go outside.
symptom_reasoning.S007: She reports forgetting books and homework in grade school.

turns.doctor_question: As an adult, before these recent memory concerns, did you also have ongoing trouble staying organized in everyday life?
turns.patient_response: Yes. It’s gotten worse lately, but I’ve always had trouble keeping everyday things organized. Papers pile up, I make lists and then don’t finish them, and I’ll sit there trying to sort things out and not know where to start. It can take me all day and still feel like nothing got done.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly reports longstanding difficulty organizing everyday items and tasks, including accumulating papers, unfinished lists, and not knowing where to start.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling down or depressed مؤخراً?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure I’d call it depressed. I get frustrated and upset with myself sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed feeling down in that way recently.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient says they have not noticed feeling down in that way recently.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about things now and then like anybody, but I haven’t noticed myself worrying a lot about all kinds of things.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient states that they have not noticed worrying a lot about many different things.

turns.doctor_question: Do you now need help with things like paying bills, managing medications, or keeping track of appointments that you used to handle on your own?
turns.patient_response: Yes. More than I used to. My daughter has started double-checking my bills and appointments because she doesn’t really trust that I’ll keep it all straight anymore. And I had to give up leading a big event at the senior center because it was just too much to manage.

symptom_reasoning.S005: She reports needing her daughter to double-check bills and appointments and having to stop leading a large event because it was too much to manage.

turns.doctor_question: Compared with a few years ago, have your memory problems clearly gotten worse?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I think they have. It’s clearer now in everyday things. I’ll miss returning calls, or I’ll find bills sitting under a stack of mail that I meant to take care of. I’ve forgotten errands I promised my daughter I’d do, and more than once I realized too late that I never confirmed one of my husband’s appointments. It’s been happening more than it used to.

symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient reports worsening everyday forgetfulness, including missed calls, unattended bills, forgotten errands, and unconfirmed appointments.

turns.doctor_question: Have there been times when your confusion or memory problems came on suddenly or got much worse during an illness or after a medical problem?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure. I can’t think of a time where it suddenly came on because I was sick or after some medical problem. It feels more like it’s just been there and gotten worse over time.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever get lost in places that used to be familiar to you?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed getting lost in places I know. I might feel a little unsure sometimes, but not like I can’t find my way somewhere familiar.

turns.doctor_question: Have your thinking and memory problems worsened in sudden steps, rather than gradually over time?
turns.patient_response: No, I don’t think it’s been in sudden steps. At least, I haven’t noticed it that way. It feels more like it’s been gradually getting worse over time.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you speak?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve really noticed a problem with finding words when I’m talking. Maybe once in a while I pause, but nothing that stands out to me.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had trouble judging where things are in space, like parking the car or using familiar objects correctly?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed trouble with judging space like that. Parking is about the same for me, and I don’t think I’m using familiar things wrong.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been getting confused about the date or what day of the week it is?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I might have to think for a second sometimes, but I’m not usually confused about the day or the date.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had to stop driving because of these thinking or memory problems?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven’t had to stop driving because of that. I’m still driving.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been diagnosed with any brain or nervous system illness, such as a stroke, Parkinson’s disease, or a head injury?
turns.patient_response: No, not that I know of. I haven’t been diagnosed with anything like a stroke or Parkinson’s, and I don’t think I’ve had a head injury.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself asking the same question again because you forgot the answer you were just given?
turns.patient_response: Not that I’ve noticed, no. I mean, I might ask for clarification if I didn’t hear something right, but I don’t think I’m repeating the same question because I forgot the answer.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been forgetting important events from your own past that you used to remember well?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I mean, I may not recall every little detail, but I haven’t noticed forgetting big events from my past that I used to remember.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel your attention and organization are clearly worse now than they were for most of your adult life?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I’d say it’s worse now. It’s been causing me this much trouble for about a year and three months, since my husband started needing regular help with his appointments and daily arrangements.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient states that their attention is clearly worse now and has been causing substantial trouble for about a year and three months.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient affirms that their organization is worse now and has been causing substantial trouble for about a year and three months.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often forget something shortly after you’ve been told it, even when you were paying attention?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure I’d say that happens often. If I’m really paying attention, I usually remember what I was just told. Sometimes I need things repeated, but I don’t know that it’s because I forgot it right away.
